items.title: 'Selling false hope': How mums are getting lured into a shampoo business
items.description: Sellers for this multi-level marketing company promise sisterhood, success and a more flexible life. But former insiders say the reality for most, is far from what’s being sold on social media.

items.title: This woman sued for pregnancy discrimination and won. Her case is rare
items.description: Research shows pregnant women and new mothers are routinely let go from their jobs, discriminated against, and, in one case, forced to pump breastmilk in a storeroom. We want to hear your stories.

items.title: A reluctant Albanese is under pressure over telehealth for VAD
items.description: At last week's Labor conference, which was totally under the prime minister's thumb, only one issue was contested on the floor: support for the use of telehealth in voluntary assisted dying care.

items.title: Ease of chargebacks crippling small businesses as banks fail to take responsibility
items.description: Despite evidence proving a customer accidentally lodged a chargeback, the bank denied the dispute from a small business owner. It raises the question of what protections are in place for this modern type of fraud.

items.title: Chinese e-commerce site selling Australian police gear
items.description: Australian police uniforms and badges are being sold on a major Chinese online shopping platform as authorities warn of a growing wave of impersonation scams.

items.title: Live: Aussies make golden start to cycling, Kennedy through to 200m final
items.description: Australia's track cycling squad has claimed three golds on the first day of competition at the velodrome, as Lachie Kennedy and Torrie Lewis feature on another packed evening of athletics. Follow live.

items.title: 'Her skin is bleeding': Devastating virus wreaks havoc in Gaza
items.description: As chickenpox spreads through Gaza's tent camps, the race to contain the virus is made harder by a lack of sanitation, overcrowding and summer heat.

items.title: Labor warns One Nation terror laws would not survive High Court
items.description: Former home affairs secretary Mike Pezzullo said there is merit in a "compromise" approach to the current process of allowing temporarily excluded Australian citizens back into the country.

items.title: Parents of Australian facing possible death penalty in Syria question confession
items.description: The family of a Gold Coast man who has been charged with murder over the death of an Australian in Syria is frustrated by the lack of progress made by the federal government in the case.

items.title: The major parties boycotted this UK by-election. Enter Count Binface
items.description: A novelty candidate called Count Binface will next month try and unseat one of the most prominent politicians in the Untied Kingdom when constituents in Clacton-on-Sea head the polls.

items.title: Albanese's absence looms large over Garma
items.description: The theme of this year's Garma Festival is "bukmak", a Yolŋu word meaning "everyone", but the prime minister's decision not to attend may indicate how high on the government's priority list Indigenous affairs sit.

items.title: 'Take them seriously': CFMEU administrator on Setka threats
items.description: CFMEU administrator Michael Crosby has opened up on threats from John Setka, cast doubt on a statement made by former Victorian premier Jacinta Allan and questioned the value of royal commissions.

items.title: Pilbara traditional owners set to appeal Fortescue's $150m native title penalty
items.description: Yindjibarndi native title holders have voted to continue their decades-long legal battle with mining billionaire Andrew Forrest.

items.title: Friday news quiz: Neil the seal's damage bill, unusual birthing methods and three premiers in one day
items.description: You too could find yourself named interim premier of Victoria if you can hold your own in today's news quiz.

items.title: The Strokes, Charli XCX, Jack White: who had the best album of July?
items.description: Blockbuster acts might have grabbed music headlines but it was Australian artists that had some of the best new releases of the month.

items.title: This exhibition will help you 'feel a little less lonely'
items.description: So many people around the world are lonely. But how do you capture the feeling? A new exhibition brings together 11 artists, including Lucy Liu, to make you less lonely.

items.title: FIFA wants to sell the World Cup to a Trump associate. Here's what we know
items.description: Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in FIFA's events and competitions arm to investors would grant them control over the World Cup and has drawn condemnation from the organising confederations.

items.title: 'Sadness' falls across coastal community after double murder-suicide
items.description: Volunteers from a regional SA town answered the call when the alarm was raised to search for a missing mother and her children.

items.title: Opposition senators say 'PM must act today' on Labor MP charged with assault
items.description: Federal Labor MP Luke Gosling has been charged with assaulting NT Administrator David Connolly, the territory equivalent of a state governor, at a festival earlier this month.

items.title: Cats hold off Magpies comeback for critical MCG win
items.description: Geelong bursts out of the gates and then holds off Collingwood's fightback for a critical 25-point win at the MCG.

items.title: Roosters put up 82 points for highest NRL score in 91 years
items.description: The Roosters have scored the third-most points ever seen in Australian rugby league first grade match and beaten the clock against a hapless North Queensland side.

items.title: A turbulent week in Victorian politics has Canberra on high alert
items.description: With a new premier installed in Victoria there are questions about what the state's electoral situation could mean federally, for all parties.

items.title: Nauru officially changes name to Naoero
items.description: Nauru has officially changed its name to Naoero, the government has announced.

items.title: US strikes 'dozens of targets' in Iran as war threatens to engulf Middle East
items.description: America's military strikes "dozens" of Revolutionary Guard targets across Iran, as the spread of hostilities to Egypt, Iraq and Saudi Arabia threatens to plunge the rest of the Middle East into all-out conflict.

items.title: Why China's memory chips could help end 'RAMageddon'
items.description: China's leading memory chip maker CXMT is emerging as a potential alternative source of memory for a market under strain from the AI boom, observers say.
